channel.title: Brain Log
channel.description: Rayed Rahman's Brain Log: Google Cybersecurity course notes, project write-ups, AGS internship work, and Arch Linux system logs.

item.title: Arch + Hyprland, Part 4: Moving to Lua Config, and a BSOD Lock Screen
item.description: An update broke my wallpaper and deprecated my config, so I moved Hyprland to its new Lua config, fixed a startup race, and rebuilt the lock screen.

item.title: Course 4: Linux and SQL
item.description: Operating systems, the Linux command line, permissions, and querying databases with SQL.

item.title: Course 3: Networks and Network Security
item.description: Network structure, protocols, common network attacks, and hardening.

item.title: TRKT: A $0 QR Ticketing and Check-in System on Cloudflare Workers
item.description: A reusable QR ticketing system I run my events on. One Worker file, one KV namespace, no monthly bill, and a check-in race condition I had to design around.

item.title: Arch + Hyprland, Part 3: Docked, Dual Monitor, and Laptop-Only Modes
item.description: Three display setups on a hybrid-GPU laptop, which four files change for each one, and how both GPUs share the work in dual-monitor mode.

item.title: Arch + Hyprland, Part 2: Rebuilding a Stable NVIDIA Setup After a Crash
item.description: After a crash I rebuilt the setup around the NVIDIA open driver, dropped the display manager, fixed a garbled TTY, and wrote down how to recover when it breaks.

item.title: rydr.info: GitHub Pages, a Custom Domain, and a DNS Rabbit Hole
item.description: How I put a hand-written HTML/CSS/JS site on GitHub Pages under my own domain, and the two DNS problems on my own network that made it look broken.

item.title: Scoping My First Web Vulnerability Assessment
item.description: The checklist I built for my first real vulnerability assessment of a Cloudflare-fronted website, based on OWASP WSTG v4.2, PTES, and NIST SP 800-115.

item.title: PING: Moving My Receipt Printer App to a Dedicated Ubuntu Server
item.description: PING prints messages people send me on a thermal receipt printer. This is the step-by-step plan for moving it off my desktop onto a proper Ubuntu LTS server.

item.title: Course 5: Assets, Threats, and Vulnerabilities
item.description: Asset security, risk planning, threat modeling, and the vulnerabilities attackers look for.

item.title: Course 2: Play It Safe, Manage Security Risks
item.description: CISSP domains, threats vs risks vs vulnerabilities, NIST frameworks, audits, SIEM tools, and playbooks.

item.title: Course 1: Foundations of Cybersecurity
item.description: Security history, the main attack types, ethics, and the roles that make up a security team.

item.title: Building a 50-Challenge CTF Platform for a National Cyber Drill
item.description: How I built, branded, and ran the CTF platform for the 2nd Agile Cyber Drill 2026 with CTFd, Docker Compose, a Flask challenge backend, and Cloudflare Tunnel.

item.title: Arch + Hyprland, Part 1: First Setup on a Laptop with an External Monitor
item.description: Getting the login screen onto my external monitor instead of the closed laptop panel, plus the clipboard, screenshot, lock, idle, wallpaper, and greeter setup I started with.
